done_when: A process's recorded start time is read the same way whatever the caller's TZ, LANG or LC_ALL, so every Forge process agrees whether a run is still alive; entries recorded by the previous release are not dropped just because their stored start text was written in another format (they keep their place while their pid runs); forge stop's verification uses the same reading; a command test starts a waiting run under one TZ and locale, reads the lanes from a Forge process under another, and shows the run keeps its place, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: The new `UTC ` prefix is incompatible with readers still running the previous release. Raw base `7800830d4e71e532bafbeda348ac126057e94ad1` confirms that its `codex.identity` returns unprefixed text and its `_queue` compares that text against every stored entry before rewriting the shared queue. Thus, an older waiting process, `forge lanes` invocation, or finishing predecessor (`src/forge/machine.py:145`; `src/forge/review.py:345`) removes live entries created by this branch—even when both callers use UTC/C. This affects both agent and test lanes: newer waiters receive “This run was stopped while waiting,” and running commands lose their reservations. The legacy tests only rewrite records belonging to commands launched with the new implementation, so they miss this interaction. Preserve newer records against previous-release readers and cover an actual old-process/new-waiter scenario. This raw-parent reader evidence is separate from the ruling to retain unverifiable old start text while its PID runs.
findings.title: Not done: Live previous-release processes can still prune newer lane entries

why: Live runs vanish from the machine's shared agent and test lanes ('This run was stopped while waiting', twice on 2026-10-08/09) because codex.identity reads a process's start time from ps -o lstart, whose text depends on the caller's TZ and locale (e.g. 'Fri 9 Oct 02:49:51' vs 'Thu 8 Oct 21:19:51' under TZ=UTC vs 'Fri Oct 9' under LANG=C); any Forge process started with a different environment (the Claude Code mod's refresh, git hooks run with a bare PATH, a pinned release run through uv) sees a mismatch and prunes the live entry as a reused pid
